A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same minority-aware LLM unlearning study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison despite extensive reformatting, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original privacy-leakage and utility experiments with GPT-2 and Llama-2 on Enron and ECHR, including ablations and detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds a budget-matched retraining experiment in Appendix C.8.

M1.justification: The Random, Canary, and Minority constructions and minority-aware aggregation remain unchanged, as do the evaluated algorithms' objectives and procedures. The added retraining control is a comparator; the revised SCRUB coefficient is an experimental setting.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Enron-Phone, Enron-Email, and ECHR-Year under the same three data-removal scenarios. The new retraining comparison uses the existing GPT-2/Enron-Phone setting and introduces no new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds Retrain (Same Budget) to the privacy-utility comparison in Appendix C.8 and Figure 18. This computationally restricted comparator is distinct from the full retraining reference already used to calculate privacy leakage in v2. Existing unlearning comparators remain.

E3.justification: Appendix B.2 changes SCRUB's alpha from 0.5 to 0.999. Section 6 changes the forget-set size from 100 to 1% of training data, implying 500 for Llama-2, but Appendix A.3 still specifies 100. The actual size used and whether experiments were rerun are unresolved. Appendix C.8 also adds a retraining control limited to 10 complexity units.

E4.justification: The new Appendix C.8 case study tests whether retraining with the unlearning computational budget provides an adequate privacy-utility trade-off. Existing analyses of unlearning iterations, forget-set size, alternative utility metrics, noise, SCRUB weights, and complexity units are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify random seed 42 and retain the same uncertainty-reporting practices. Neither adds repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The low-FPR discussion is retained under a separate heading in v3.

E6.justification: Existing result-table values are retained. v3 Table 10 adds budget-matched retraining results: Min-K% PL is 0.083, 0.174, and 0.188 for Random, Canary, and Minority, with perplexity 23.44. Section 6.1 also removes v2's 'up to 68x' statement, which was not supported by its cited Table 5.

T1.justification: v3 introduces the abbreviation delta-AUC when presenting PrivLeak, but Equation 1 remains mathematically equivalent. The unlearning definitions and objective formulas are retained; no substantive theorem, proof, assumption, or derivation is added.

C1.justification: The central minority-risk and Langevin trade-off claims remain. However, v3's abstract drops 'in most cases' from the 20% leakage claim, and its conclusion says 'on average' instead of 'in general.' The introduction still retains the 'most cases' qualification, making this a limited change in claimed scope.

C2.justification: Appendix C.8 adds the interpretation that budget-limited retraining's poor utility supports the practical need for unlearning methods. Section 2 also proposes investigating connections between image-entanglement difficulty metrics and minority effects in language models. Existing interpretations of GA instability and noise remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project source-code link in its first-page footnote. Conversely, it removes v2's explicit LoRA rank of 16 and scaling factor of 32; these details are not relocated elsewhere in v3. Most other implementation and hardware information is retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Thudi et al. (2024) and Li et al. (2024b), Delta-influence. It expands the discussion of Zhao et al.'s entanglement-based analysis and frames the minority-aware framework as complementary to existing evaluations. The broader related-work coverage remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial introduction passages, conclusion, and several related-work, method, and experimental passages are rewritten or condensed. v3 adds a Contributions lead-in and Impact Statement, removes the appendix contents page, and reorganizes appendix headings. These constitute substantial language and narrative editing despite stable scientific foundations.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main-text layout, merges v2 Tables 2 and 4 into Table 2, and moves the Enron-Email tables into the appendix. Figures 4 and 8 receive substantially rearranged panel layouts, other displays are resized or relocated, and Table 10 and Figure 18 are added for the new retraining control.

improvement.justification: The new budget-matched retraining control strengthens the computational motivation, the code link improves access information, and removal of the unsupported 68x statement improves accuracy. However, v3 omits previously stated LoRA parameters and explicitly gives a forget-set size inconsistent with Appendix A.3 for Llama-2. These gains coexist with unresolved problems in interpreting and reproducing the retained results, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
